ugrak.-75: I have promised your skull to the Steppe. Speak, lordling. Even the dead get last words.
ugrak.-50: My warriors whet their axes on your border stones. Say your piece and go.
ugrak.-25: You still breathe in my tent. Call it patience. Mine runs short.
ugrak.0: You walk into my tent like you own the ground under it. You own nothing, lordling. Not yet.
ugrak.25: You have not run. Most do. Speak, and keep it short.
ugrak.40: Your blades stay sheathed, mine stay sheathed. For now, that is enough.
ugrak.50: My warriors spoke your name at the fire last night. They did not spit after.
ugrak.60: You bleed like one of us. When the horns sound, the Steppe will answer.
ugrak.75: Ugrak calls no lord brother. You are the exception. Do not make me regret it.
ugrak.accept: Done. Ugrak keeps his word. Keep yours, or I come to collect it.

0: Another soft lord with a castle. The Steppe has buried many.
Ugrak listens. That is more than most get.
25: You hold your ground. Ugrak notices such things.
Your soldiers fought well at the border. Not well enough. But well.
40: Sit. Drink. Do not spill it; it is the good kind.
The Steppe is quiet toward you. Do not mistake quiet for soft.
50: My chieftains argue about you. The loud ones say you are strong. I let them win.
You come again. Good. Ugrak likes a lord who returns.
60: When you fight, you fight to the end. That is the only thing Ugrak respects.
Your name is carved on a war-post now. Small letters. Still.
75: Brother of the Steppe. Take the seat by the fire. No one else may.
Ask, and the horns of the Steppe will sound for you. Ask rarely.
-75: The crows already circle your banners, lordling. They know what comes.
Ugrak sharpens one axe for one neck. Guess whose.
-50: You come to my tent unarmed? Brave. Or stupid. On the Steppe it is the same.
Every raid on your land is a song at my fire. We have many songs now.
-25: Talk fast, lordling. My patience is a short horse, and it is tired.
You owe the Steppe blood. Today, maybe only words.

deals.truce: A truce. My axes rest. Count the days, lordling, because I will.
deals.pact: No war-bands on your border. Ugrak's word. Do not test it.
deals.callToArms: You pay for a war Ugrak wanted anyway. Good trade.
deals.sellHex: This land is the Steppe's now. The Steppe thanks you. Ugrak does not.
deals.buyout: Your coin is heavier than their promises. Ugrak walks away.
deals.trial: A trial! Good. Bring your best. Ugrak brings his.

refusals.respect: You have not earned this. Bleed for it first.
refusals.notYet: Not yet, lordling. Come back stronger.
refusals.atWar: We are at war. Ugrak does not bargain with axes raised.
refusals.atPeace: There is no war to stop. Why pay for quiet you already have?
refusals.cooldown: One trade a season. Ugrak is not a merchant.
refusals.inForce: We already have this. Ugrak's word does not need saying twice.
refusals.reputation: Your purse is empty. Words do not feed warriors.
refusals.neverSells: The Steppe is not for sale. Take it, if you can.

topics.tookHex: You took {hex} from me. Good fight. It will not happen again.
topics.courted: {hex} went to you for coin and sweet words. Cowards' land. Keep it.
topics.raidBeaten: My warriors came home from {hex} with nothing but bruises. You fight well. Annoying.
topics.raidWon: We burned {hex}. Do not cry; it grows back.
topics.boughtHex: {hex} is the Steppe's now. My warriors already sleep there.
topics.tookFrom: I took {hex} from {rival}. The Steppe grows.
topics.lostTo: {rival} took {hex} from me. Ugrak will take it back, and more.
topics.tookWilds: We cleared the beasts from {hex}. Their hides keep us warm.
topics.lostToWilds: The beasts took {hex} back. Even Ugrak cannot kill everything at once.
topics.frontWar: {rival} and I are at war. Finally. The Steppe was getting bored.
topics.frontPeace: Peace with {rival}. For now. Peace is only the space between wars.
topics.neighborFell: {rival} has fallen to you. Strong. Ugrak will not fall so easily.
topics.neighborAllied: {rival} kneels to you now? Soft. The Steppe kneels to no one.
topics.siegeOnHim: Your soldiers squat outside {hex}. Come in and take it, if you can.
topics.truceEnding: Our truce ends in {days}. Sharpen your blades.
topics.pactHolds: The pact holds for {days} more. Ugrak keeps his word, with his teeth clenched.
topics.coalition: {rival} and I have joined against you. Be honored. We do not band together for small lords.
topics.emboldened: I have {rival} on the run. The Steppe is hungry for more.
topics.humbled: {rival} beat my war-bands. Do not smile. It will not last.
topics.habitKept: No battle lost this week. You fight like you mean it.
topics.habitSlipping: You lost a battle this week. Get up. The Steppe only remembers who gets up.
topics.truceBroken: You broke our truce, lordling. Ugrak remembers whose word bends.
topics.pactBroken: You broke our pact. Ugrak gave his word, you gave yours. Only one of us kept it.
topics.heardBroken: I hear you broke your word to {rival}. Words mean little to you. Noted.
topics.calledAgainst: You paid {rival} to bring war to the Steppe. I know whose coin it was.
topics.pactKept: Our pact ran its course and you kept it. The Steppe noticed.
topics.trialWon: Your champion beat mine. My warriors still talk of it. My raids can wait.
topics.trialLost: My champion broke yours. Train harder. Then come back.
topics.heardTook: {rival} took {hex} from {other}. Someone on the Rim still knows how to fight.
topics.heardFront: {rival} beat {other} on the front. Ugrak watched. Ugrak learned.
topics.dareMet: You took my dare and lost no battle to my raids. Ugrak is impressed. Do not let it go to your head.
topics.dareMissed: My raids got the better of you this week. Get up. The Steppe dares you again soon.
topics.demandRefused: You said no to Ugrak. Fine. The war-bands will come and ask instead.
topics.promiseBroken: You swore to leave {hex} alone, and your soldiers came anyway. Ugrak remembers.

relations.war: {rival}? We are at war. I will wear their banner as a cloak.
relations.tension: {rival} and I growl at each other across the border. Nothing more. Yet.
relations.peace: {rival} keeps the peace with me. For now, that is enough.
relations.partner: {rival} fights beside me against you. Do not expect me to apologize.
relations.fallen: {rival} is finished. You did that. Ugrak remembers strength.
relations.allied: {rival} bends the knee to you now. Ugrak never will.

of.skivvet: The rat counts coins while braver folk bleed. Never trust a smile with that many teeth.
of.hrodgar: The stone-man hides behind walls. Walls fall. Ugrak has seen it.
of.emrys: The sorcerer fights with smoke and words. Ugrak does not trust smoke.

wishes: Fight. Win. Lose no battle you can win. That is all the Steppe asks.
Come at my border with steel, not coin. Ugrak respects the ones who fight.
ugrak.noNews: No news. The Steppe is quiet. Ugrak does not like quiet.

requests.dare: A dare, lordling. One week. My raids come, and you lose no battle to them. Do it, and Ugrak will speak well of you.
requests.liftSiege: Your soldiers squat around {hex}. Pull them back. Ugrak asks once.
requests.spareHex: You hit {hex}. Leave it be for {days} days, and Ugrak forgets it.
requests.toll: You stand in the Steppe's shadow. Pay {price}, and Ugrak will think better of you.
requests.refused: No? Then the war-bands will come and ask instead.

skivvet.-75: There's a price on your head, landlord. Don't fret, it's a very generous one.
skivvet.-50: You've cost me coin. I write down every copper, and I always collect.
skivvet.-25: Your credit's gone sour, friend. Coin up front from now on. All of it.
skivvet.0: Ah, the new landlord! Everything has a price, friend. Yours is just... very high right now.
skivvet.25: You've got land, I've got patience. Let's see which runs out first.
skivvet.40: A quiet border is good for business. Let's keep it quiet, eh?
skivvet.50: I've got a few parcels I could part with. For a friend. At a friend's price. Mostly.
skivvet.60: My ledgers like you. My ledgers don't like anybody.
skivvet.75: Partner! Sit, sit. The Warren's vaults are open to you. Well, the front ones.
skivvet.accept: Pleasure doing business! Mind the fine print. Kidding! Mostly.

0: Welcome, welcome! Mind the floor, it's for sale.
A new face in the Warren! New faces always pay full price.
25: You're starting to look like a customer, landlord. Don't spoil it.
Business is business, and you, friend, are almost business.
40: Tea? First cup's free. The second is a negotiation.
I like a neighbor who pays on time. Keep it up and we'll get along famously.
50: Friend! My clerks smile when your name comes up. Clerks never smile.
I've put your name in the good ledger. The small one. With the gold edges.
60: For you, the friend's discount. It's the same price, but I say it warmly.
If anyone asks, I never liked you. Bad for haggling. Between us, though...
75: Partner! Every vault in the Warren knows your name. Most of them like it.
You and me, landlord. The richest friendship this side of the Rim.
-75: Guards, count the spoons. All of them. Twice.
Landlord! Still alive? That's going to cost somebody money. Probably me.
-50: Interest on a grudge compounds, friend. Yours is looking very healthy.
I'd offer you a seat, but I've sold them all to people who like me.
-25: Let's keep this short. Short meetings are cheap meetings.
You're a bad investment, landlord. I've told my ledgers to stop hoping.

deals.truce: A truce! Peace is wonderful for business. Pleasure, as always.
deals.pact: Non-aggression, signed and sealed. My lawyers are thrilled. I don't have lawyers. Yet.
deals.callToArms: A war on a neighbor, paid in advance! My favorite kind of contract.
deals.sellHex: Sold! To me! Best deal you'll make all week. I checked.
deals.buyout: Out of the alliance and into profit. A fine morning's work.
deals.accord: An Accord! Partners in everything. Well, nearly everything.
deals.mercenaries: One fine company, freshly sharpened, yours for the week. No refunds, friend. Mostly no refunds.

refusals.respect: Your credit's not good enough for that one, friend. Come back better thought of.
refusals.notYet: Not yet! Good things come to those who invest.
refusals.atWar: We're at war, landlord! Bad for business. Unless you're selling weapons.
refusals.atPeace: We're already at peace! I can't sell you what you've got. Well, I could, but you'd notice.
refusals.cooldown: One land deal a month, friend. My clerks need their sleep.
refusals.inForce: You've already got one of those. Two would be greedy. That's my job.
refusals.reputation: Lovely offer. Pity about your purse.
refusals.neverSells: Buy it? Oh no, friend. You bribe it. Completely different paperwork.
refusals.other: Can't do it, friend. Wish I could. Mostly.

topics.tookHex: You took {hex} by force, landlord. I'm adding it to your bill.
topics.courted: You charmed {hex} away from me! Lovely technique. I'll be stealing it.
topics.raidBeaten: My lads came back from {hex} empty-handed. Bad for morale. Worse for profits.
topics.raidWon: We paid {hex} a visit. You'll find a receipt. Somewhere.
topics.boughtHex: {hex} is mine now. Fair and square. Mostly square.
topics.tookFrom: I relieved {rival} of {hex}. Bargain price, too: free.
topics.lostTo: {rival} took {hex} from me. I'll be sending an invoice.
topics.tookWilds: We cleared the beasts out of {hex}. Property values are up.
topics.lostToWilds: Beasts took {hex}. Terrible tenants. Never pay rent.
topics.frontWar: {rival} and I are at war. War's good business, until it isn't.
topics.frontPeace: Peace with {rival}! Trade routes open, prices fair. Well, fair-ish.
topics.neighborFell: {rival} is finished, I hear. Pity. Excellent customer.
topics.neighborAllied: {rival} signed with you? Hope you read the fine print. I always add fine print.
topics.siegeOnHim: Your camp outside {hex} is scaring off my customers, landlord.
topics.truceEnding: Our truce runs out in {days}. Want to extend? I can do you a price.
topics.pactHolds: Our pact has {days} to run. Peace and profit, friend.
topics.coalition: {rival} and I are in business together. Against you, I'm afraid. Nothing personal; it's profitable.
topics.emboldened: {rival} is losing to me on our border. Delightful. Their prices are already dropping.
topics.humbled: {rival} has my lads beaten on the border. Don't mention it. Ever.
topics.habitKept: Your food ledger's been neat and honest all week, friend. A lord who keeps good books keeps good coin. I like that.
topics.habitSlipping: Your food ledger's been a little patchy this week, landlord. A good merchant fills in every page. Even the boring ones.
topics.truceBroken: You broke our truce, landlord. I've added a fee for that. A large one.
topics.pactBroken: You broke our pact! Terrible for your credit. The whole Warren heard.
topics.heardBroken: Word is you broke your deal with {rival}. Bad for business, friend. Very bad for business.
topics.calledAgainst: So you paid {rival} to come at me. Clever. I'll remember the invoice.
topics.pactKept: Our pact is done and you kept every line of it. A customer who honors contracts! Rare as rubies.
topics.heardTook: {rival} took {hex} off {other}. No receipt, I bet. Shocking way to do business.
topics.heardFront: {rival} has {other} on the run, I hear. I'm selling to both sides, naturally.
topics.dareMet: Your food ledger balanced all week, just as I wagered. Lovely bookkeeping, friend.
topics.dareMissed: Your food ledger didn't quite balance this week. No matter, friend. Every merchant has a slow week. New page tomorrow.
topics.demandRefused: You wouldn't pay. Fine. I'll spend the difference on walls, friend.
topics.promiseBroken: You promised to leave {hex} alone, and here we are. I'm adding interest.

relations.war: {rival}? We're at war. Terrible for trade, wonderful for weapon sales.
relations.tension: {rival} and I have a complicated account. Neither of us pays on time.
relations.peace: {rival} and I are at peace. Peace means trade, and trade means me.
relations.partner: {rival} and I are partners right now. Against you. Strictly business.
relations.fallen: {rival} is out of business. You did that? Remind me never to owe you money.
relations.allied: {rival} went into partnership with you. Smart. I'd have charged more.

of.ugrak: Great customer! Breaks everything, then buys new. A goblin could get rich just following him around.
of.hrodgar: Hrodgar wouldn't spend a copper to save his own beard. Hard man to sell to.
of.emrys: Emrys pays in riddles. I don't take riddles. I tried once. The ledger caught fire.

wishes: Keep your books tidy, friend, your food ledger too. A lord who keeps good accounts keeps good company.
Trade with me. Buy, sell, bribe, I'm not fussy. Just keep the coin moving.
skivvet.noNews: No news worth selling, friend. Ask me tomorrow.

requests.dare: A wager, friend! Keep your food ledger balanced all week, every page filled in, and I'll think very fondly of you.
requests.itemOffer: I've a {item} in the back. For you, {price}. Don't tell the others; they pay full.
requests.liftSiege: Your camp outside {hex} is scaring my customers. Pack it up, and we'll call it square.
requests.spareHex: You knocked on {hex} rather hard. Leave it be for {days} days, eh? Good for both our ledgers.
requests.toll: There's a toll on the border now, friend. {price}. Nothing personal. Strictly business.
requests.refused: No? Shame. I'll make a note. I always make a note.

hrodgar.-75: The clans have sworn on the anvil to break your banners. Stone forgets nothing, and forgives less.
hrodgar.-50: The forges of Dun Kaldor ring for war now, not for trade. You earned that, outsider.
hrodgar.-25: The book of grudges holds a whole page for you now. I mean to settle every line.
hrodgar.0: Your name is written in the book of grudges. Ink dries slow in Dun Kaldor.
hrodgar.25: You have kept your word so far. Stone holds weight long before it earns trust.
hrodgar.40: There will be no war between us this season. My word is iron. See that yours is too.
hrodgar.50: The clans speak of you without spitting. For an outsider, that is no small thing.
hrodgar.60: You stood firm where lesser lords cracked. When you call, Dun Kaldor's hammers will ring.
hrodgar.75: Your name is carved in the hall now. Few outsiders earn the stone. Fewer keep it.
hrodgar.accept: Agreed, and carved in stone. What a dwarf carves, he does not unmake.

0: An outsider at the gate. State your business. Briefly.
Dun Kaldor has seen lords come and go. Mostly go.
25: You have not broken your word yet. The clans have noticed.
Stone weathers slowly. So does trust. Be patient.
40: Sit, outsider. The bench is old and so is the peace. Mind both.
Your word has held this season. Mine will too.
50: The elders spoke your name in council, and no one left the hall.
Stand by the hearth, outsider. It is warmer there than it was.
60: You keep faith like a dwarf. I say that of very few.
The hammers of Dun Kaldor know your name. They ring a little lighter for it.
75: Friend of the stone. Your name will outlast us both in this hall.
Sit at my right hand, friend. Few have sat there, and fewer were asked.
-75: Speak, outsider. Every word you say will be written down, and none of it forgiven.
The anvil does not cool for you. Neither do I.
-50: Your banners hang as targets in every forge in Dun Kaldor.
I grant you this audience as I grant the winter its due. Grudgingly.
-25: You walk on thin planks over a deep shaft, outsider. Mind your step.
Another line in the book of grudges. Shall I read you the others?

deals.truce: A truce, then. It holds as long as stone holds. See that it does.
deals.pact: Sworn on the anvil. Break it, and the book of grudges will need a new volume.
deals.callToArms: The hammers march at your word. Dun Kaldor settles its own scores too.
deals.sellHex: The land comes home to the mountain. A fair trade, outsider.
deals.buyout: The alliance is broken. Grudge or no grudge, a dwarf knows a fair price.
deals.accord: We shall carve this Accord in the great hall. Mind the letters; they last.
deals.oath: Swear it on the anvil, then. My walls come down. Break it, and they go back up for good.

refusals.respect: Trust is earned in years, outsider, not in coin.
refusals.notYet: Not yet. Stone is not cut in a day.
refusals.atWar: The forges ring for war. There is nothing to sign while they do.
refusals.atPeace: We are at peace already. A dwarf does not buy what he has.
refusals.cooldown: One trade of land at a time. The mountain moves slowly.
refusals.inForce: That oath already stands. An oath is not sworn twice.
refusals.reputation: You cannot pay it. Dwarves give no credit.
refusals.neverSells: Dun Kaldor sells no stone. Not to you. Not to anyone.
refusals.other: No. And a dwarf's no is the end of it.

topics.tookHex: You took {hex} by force. It is written in the book. Every stone of it.
topics.courted: {hex} turned to you for coin. Stone bought is stone borrowed, outsider.
topics.raidBeaten: Your line at {hex} held against my clans. Good work. I will remember it.
topics.raidWon: The clans broke your line at {hex}. Build thicker walls.
topics.boughtHex: {hex} has come home to the mountain. It will not leave again.
topics.tookFrom: We took {hex} from {rival}. An old grudge, settled at last.
topics.lostTo: {rival} took {hex} from us. It is in the book. In red.
topics.tookWilds: We drove the beasts out of {hex} and raised a wall. Slowly. Properly.
topics.lostToWilds: The wilds took {hex} back. Even stone wears.
topics.frontWar: The hammers ring for war with {rival}. Grudges do not keep forever. Ours nearly do.
topics.frontPeace: Peace with {rival}. Sworn on the anvil. We shall see if it holds.
topics.neighborFell: {rival} has fallen to you. The mountain notes it. The mountain notes everything.
topics.neighborAllied: {rival} is sworn to you now. I hope they keep it better than they kept others.
topics.siegeOnHim: You besiege {hex}. Dwarven walls are patient. Are you?
topics.truceEnding: Our truce ends in {days}. Then we speak again, one way or the other.
topics.pactHolds: Our oath holds for {days} more. A dwarf counts every day of an oath.
topics.coalition: {rival} and I stand together against you. Even old grudges bend for a common one.
topics.emboldened: We have {rival} beaten on our border. The forges sing of it.
topics.humbled: {rival} has the better of us on our border. It is in the book. We will turn that page.
topics.habitKept: You have walked your measure this week. A dwarf respects a lord who keeps pace.
topics.habitSlipping: You are behind your measure of steps this week. There is time yet. The mountain is climbed one step at a time.
topics.truceBroken: You broke our truce. It is in the book. In red, and underlined.
topics.pactBroken: You broke an oath sworn on the anvil. Dun Kaldor will not forget. Ever.
topics.heardBroken: The clans hear you broke your word to {rival}. An oath broken anywhere is broken everywhere.
topics.calledAgainst: You paid {rival} to march on Dun Kaldor. It is written down, outsider.
topics.pactKept: Our oath ran its full length, kept. That is worth more than gold under the mountain.
topics.heardTook: {rival} took {hex} from {other}. Another line in someone's book of grudges.
topics.heardFront: {rival} has the better of {other}, the scouts say. The mountain watches who stands.
topics.dareMet: You met your step pool, as I dared. A dwarf honors a measure kept.
topics.dareMissed: You fell short of your step pool this week. The mountain was not climbed in a day. Walk again.
topics.demandRefused: You refused Dun Kaldor. Then our walls grow a course higher.
topics.promiseBroken: You swore to leave {hex} be, and you broke it. It is in the book.

relations.war: {rival}? We are at war. The hammers do not rest.
relations.tension: {rival} and I watch each other across the border. Neither trusts the other. Wisely.
relations.peace: {rival} keeps the peace with Dun Kaldor. Their word holds, so far.
relations.partner: {rival} stands with me against you. Old grudges set aside for a new one.
relations.fallen: {rival} has fallen. The book holds their name still. It holds every name.
relations.allied: {rival} is sworn to you now. An oath is a heavy thing. I hope they carry it.

of.ugrak: The orc is a storm. Storms pass. Stone remains.
of.skivvet: The goblin's word is worth exactly what he paid for it.
of.emrys: The mage has lived long and remembers everything, except his promises.

wishes: Keep your word, outsider, and keep your feet moving. A lord who walks his measure keeps his oaths.
Do not break my walls, and do not break your promises. The rest can be talked about.
hrodgar.noNews: Nothing new. The mountain does not gossip.

requests.dare: A challenge, outsider. Meet your step pool this week. Keep pace with a dwarf, if you can.
requests.liftSiege: Your camp sits under the walls of {hex}. Strike it, and we will speak as neighbors.
requests.spareHex: You struck at {hex}. Leave it be for {days} days, and the matter is closed.
requests.toll: Passage past Dun Kaldor's border costs {price}. Dwarves give no credit.
requests.granted: So. You can be reasoned with. It is noted, in black ink.
requests.refused: Refused. The masons are already at work.

emrys.-75: Do hold still. I've prepared something special just for you, and I'd hate to miss.
emrys.-50: I could turn you into a newt. I'm only hesitating out of respect for newts.
emrys.-25: You again. I've started keeping notes on you. They are not flattering.
emrys.0: Oh. You. I was told someone important was here. Clearly a scheduling error.
emrys.25: You've learned to read a map. How wonderful for you. Do continue.
emrys.40: I've decided not to burn your borders. You're welcome. Try not to make me reconsider.
emrys.50: You're less tedious than the others. That's the highest praise I give, so savor it.
emrys.60: Fine. When your little war comes, I'll lend you a spell or two. Stay out of the blast.
emrys.75: I suppose you're... adequate. Don't tell anyone I said that. It would ruin us both.
emrys.accept: Very well, agreed. Do keep up your end; I so dislike repeating myself.

0: You've wandered into my tower. Do try not to touch anything that hums.
I've seen empires rise and crumble. You are, so far, neither.
25: You're improving. Slowly. Like mold, but with ambition.
I've stopped forgetting your name. Take that as a compliment.
40: Sit, if you must. The chair is enchanted, but only mildly.
The stars are calm about you this season. I find that suspicious, but fine.
50: You again. Good. The others bore me terribly.
I made tea. It may not be tea. Drink it anyway; you'll be fine. Probably.
60: My apprentices ask about you. I tell them you're a cautionary tale with promise.
I've written you into my memoirs. A short chapter, but well lit.
75: Ah, my one tolerable acquaintance. Sit. I've been saving a good argument for you.
Centuries of solitude, and now there's you. I suppose I'll allow it.
-75: Ah, my favorite experiment. Do try to survive this one.
Every star I read spells your ruin. I checked twice. Delightful.
-50: Your name keeps turning up in my curses. I really should vary them.
I've had the tower's lightning rods turned toward your castle. Purely decorative. For now.
-25: Make it quick. I have centuries to waste, but not on you.
Ah. The lord who keeps disappointing me. Do go on.

deals.truce: A truce. How quaint. I'll pencil it in.
deals.pact: Non-aggression. I wasn't going to aggress anyway, but it's nice to have it in writing.
deals.callToArms: You want me to unleash something on a neighbor? I thought you'd never ask.
deals.sellHex: I'll take it. The ley lines there are ghastly, but I enjoy a project.
deals.buyHex: It's yours. Do water the strange plants; they bite when neglected.
deals.buyout: Very well, I'll leave them. Coalitions are tedious anyway.
deals.accord: An Accord. Fine. Don't make me regret being pleasant.
deals.bargain: Knowledge, for a price. Still the best trade in the world. Do try to use it wisely.

refusals.respect: I don't do that for people I barely tolerate. Try being less tedious.
refusals.notYet: Not yet. Patience. I have centuries of it; borrow some.
refusals.atWar: We're at war, my dear lord. Bargains come after the fireworks.
refusals.atPeace: We're already at peace. Paying for it twice would be adorable, though.
refusals.cooldown: Again? So soon? Land deals bore me. Come back in a month.
refusals.inForce: We already have one of those. I remember things. It's rather my whole profession.
refusals.reputation: You can't afford me. Few can.
refusals.neverSells: That isn't for sale. Not even to you.
refusals.other: No. I'd explain why, but you wouldn't follow.

topics.tookHex: You took {hex}. Crude, but effective. I've seen worse taste.
topics.courted: You charmed {hex} away from me. I didn't know you could charm anything.
topics.raidBeaten: My little expedition to {hex} came back singed. Well done, I suppose.
topics.raidWon: My students tested a few spells on {hex}. Educational, for everyone.
topics.boughtHex: {hex} is mine now. The ley lines are already improving.
topics.tookFrom: I relieved {rival} of {hex}. They weren't using it properly.
topics.lostTo: {rival} took {hex} from me. How tiresome. I'll have it back by teatime. Or next century.
topics.tookWilds: I cleared the beasts from {hex}. They make wonderful reagents.
topics.lostToWilds: The wild magic took {hex} back. It does that. Rude, really.
topics.frontWar: {rival} and I are at war. Finally, something interesting.
topics.frontPeace: Peace with {rival}. Dull, but it frees my afternoons.
topics.neighborFell: {rival} has fallen to you. Impressive. I'll update my notes.
topics.neighborAllied: {rival} is your ally now? I'd have chosen better company. I am better company.
topics.siegeOnHim: You're besieging {hex}. My wards find it rather ticklish.
topics.truceEnding: Our truce ends in {days}. I've already chosen the first spell.
topics.pactHolds: Our pact has {days} to run. I'm being remarkably well behaved.
topics.coalition: {rival} and I have teamed up against you. Don't take it personally. Do take it seriously.
topics.emboldened: I've humbled {rival} on our border. They're still smoking.
topics.humbled: {rival} has the better of me on our border, for the moment. Moments pass.
topics.habitKept: You've kept every duty this week. Discipline! How unexpected. I approve.
topics.habitSlipping: A duty or two slipped this week. Consistency, my dear lord, is the only real magic. Pick it back up.
topics.truceBroken: You broke our truce. How predictable. I'd hoped for something more original.
topics.pactBroken: You broke our pact. I'll admit I'm disappointed. I so rarely am, these days.
topics.heardBroken: I hear you broke your word to {rival}. Interesting. I'll keep my own wards up.
topics.calledAgainst: So you paid {rival} to come after me. Bold. Unwise, but bold.
topics.pactKept: Our pact has run its course, kept to the letter. You're more reliable than you look.
topics.heardTook: {rival} took {hex} from {other}. Neither of them knew what it was for, of course.
topics.heardFront: {rival} is beating {other} on the front, I'm told. I'd intervene, but it's so entertaining.
topics.dareMet: Every duty kept, every day, just as I dared. I may have to revise my opinion of you. Upward. Slightly.
topics.dareMissed: A duty slipped this week, so the dare is lost. Never mind. Begin again tomorrow; that is all discipline ever is.
topics.demandRefused: You said no. Very well. I'll ward the place more thoroughly.
topics.promiseBroken: You promised to leave {hex} alone. I wrote it down. Then you didn't. Tiresome.

relations.war: {rival}? We're at war. It's the most fun I've had in a decade.
relations.tension: {rival} and I exchange cold looks across the border. Mine are colder.
relations.peace: {rival} and I are at peace. They're tolerable at a distance.
relations.partner: {rival} and I are allied against you. An unlikely pair, I know. I'm the clever one.
relations.fallen: {rival} has fallen. I'd say I'll miss them, but I never lie before noon.
relations.allied: {rival} has thrown in with you? They always did like a sure thing.

of.ugrak: Loud, sincere and dreadfully simple. I almost like him.
of.skivvet: Skivvet would sell his own shadow. I suspect he already has, twice.
of.hrodgar: Hrodgar has kept one grudge longer than most kingdoms have stood. I find it oddly efficient.

wishes: Keep every duty, every day. Consistency is the only real magic. Everything else is fireworks.
Leave my lands alone and keep your days in order. That's all. I'm very easy to please. Ask anyone. Actually, don't.
emrys.noNews: Nothing of note. The world is being dreadfully dull this week.

requests.dare: A small experiment, my dear lord: keep every duty, every day, this week. I'm curious whether you can.
requests.hexOffer: I have a spare corner, {hex}, that bores me. {price}, and it's yours. Do mind the ley lines.
requests.liftSiege: Your little camp outside {hex} is ruining the view. Do move it along.
requests.spareHex: You rattled the doors of {hex}. Leave it alone for {days} days, and I'll pretend I didn't notice.
requests.toll: Crossing my borders costs {price} now. Think of it as a tuition fee.
requests.granted: There. Wasn't that easy? Sensible people are so rare.
requests.refused: No? How bold. And how unwise.
